title: Sentry MCP Safe Error Monitoring Setup 2026: Secure Configuration Guide for AI Coding Agents
topic: Safe configuration and security hardening of Sentry MCP for AI coding agents — OAuth setup, token management, SSRF protection, prompt injection defenses, and monitoring best practices
targetAudience: DevOps engineers, security teams, and developers configuring Sentry MCP with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, and other AI coding agents

repoStatus.status: Actively maintained — Sentry team is actively adding security features (OAuth, SSRF protection, tool hint annotations, structured results)

authModel.remote: Two-layer OAuth: MCP OAuth (Cloudflare) wrapping upstream Sentry OAuth. Client never sees raw Sentry token.
authModel.directToken: Sentry-Bearer header for trusted clients — token passed through without storage/validation by worker
authModel.stdio: Sentry User Auth Token via SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN env var or --access-token CLI flag
authModel.scopes: org:read, project:read, project:write, team:read, team:write, event:write

trustBoundaries: Client-to-MCP: client only receives MCP token, not raw Sentry credentials
MCP-to-Sentry: only server uses upstream Sentry bearer token
Session narrowing: broad upstream scopes narrowed by MCP-side skills and URL constraints
Revocation on upstream failure: stale upstream tokens force re-authorization

permissionModel.primaryAuth: grantedSkills — which tools the session can access
permissionModel.upstreamChecks: Sentry's own bearer-token checks for underlying API operations

ssrfProtection.mechanism: validateRegionUrl() — restricts region URLs to base host + allowlist (sentry.io, us.sentry.io, de.sentry.io)
rules: Default: only base host allowed as regionUrl
Additional domains must be in SENTRY_ALLOWED_REGION_DOMAINS allowlist

currentMeasures: All tool inputs validated with Zod schemas
URLs parsed and validated before use
Region URLs restricted to known Sentry domains
No direct command execution in tools

openPRs.title: Untrusted data boundary for get_issue_details
openPRs.approach: XML boundary tags + HTML entity escaping + LLM eval canary

openPRs.title: Structured Sentry tool results
openPRs.approach: StructuredContent payloads with broad security notes

knownGaps: Unsupported event types skip untrusted data boundary
Response Notes enclosed inside untrusted boundary (tells LLM to ignore its own instructions)
Boundary only covers Description field; exception values, stack frame variables, tags raw
No field-level provenance tracking (issue #1093 debated but not implemented)

toolHintAnnotations.description: Enforcing readOnlyHint and destructiveHint annotations on all tools — part of broader MCP security hardening

oauthSecurity.stateProtection: HMAC-signed OAuth state payload with 10-minute expiry
oauthSecurity.errorHandling: No token/secret exposure in errors; generic messages for auth failures

sdkConfiguration.cloudflare: @sentry/cloudflare with DSN, environment, beforeSend redaction of auth headers

tracing.pattern: createTracedToolHandler wraps every tool with OpenTelemetry spans

embeddedAgentConfig.purpose: AI-powered search tools (search_events, search_issues, search_issue_events, use_sentry)
embeddedAgentConfig.configMethod: EMBEDDED_AGENT_PROVIDER env var (recommended) or --agent-provider CLI flag
securityConsiderations: Always set EMBEDDED_AGENT_PROVIDER explicitly when multiple API keys present
Auto-detection deprecated — prevents silent provider switching when external tools inject API keys
Claude Agent SDK injects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — explicit provider selection required to override
Custom base URLs supported for OpenAI-compatible endpoints or Anthropic proxies

claudeCodePluginSecurity.architecture: Subagent auto-delegation — Claude Code delegates to sentry-mcp subagent when user asks about errors
claudeCodePluginSecurity.allowedTools: Auto-generated from toolDefinitions.json — restricts which MCP tools the subagent can call
securityImplications: Auto-delegation means no human review before Sentry MCP tools are invoked
Subagent has full access to configured MCP tools — no per-call approval
allowedTools list is the primary restriction mechanism
Experimental variant exposes additional tools without additional consent

items: Use OAuth remote mode for production (client never sees raw Sentry token)
For stdio: use SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN env var, not hardcoded in config files
Scope tokens to minimum required orgs/projects
Use /mcp/:org or /mcp/:org/:project URL constraints to narrow token scope
Disable unnecessary skills with --disable-skills=seer or ?disable-skills=seer
Narrow direct tool exposure with ?skills=inspect,triage query parameters
Review allowedTools in Claude Code plugin — ensure only needed tools are exposed
Avoid experimental mode in production (?experimental=1)
Monitor PR #1056 (untrusted data boundary) and PR #1045 (structured results) for merge
Implement server-side relay that strips markdown/commands from error descriptions
Configure agent to require human approval for commands sourced from MCP data
Use MCP-Scan to audit connected MCP servers for tool poisoning
Configure Sentry SDK with beforeSend to redact sensitive data (auth headers, tokens)
Set appropriate tracesSampleRate (0.1 recommended for production)
Monitor for unexpected tool calls or data access patterns
Watch for 5xx errors, network failures, and rate limit errors (429)
Use app.server.response metrics grouped by route and status code
Always set EMBEDDED_AGENT_PROVIDER explicitly when multiple API keys present
Use dedicated API keys for Sentry MCP — don't share with other tools
Consider disabling AI-powered search tools if not needed (reduces attack surface)
For self-hosted: verify Seer availability before enabling AI search tools
Use HTTPS for all connections (enforced by SSRF protection)
Configure SENTRY_ALLOWED_REGION_DOMAINS if using custom Sentry regions
For self-hosted: use --insecure-http only in isolated internal deployments
Validate region URLs are restricted to known Sentry domains
Set SENTRY_CLIENT_ID and SENTRY_CLIENT_SECRET for OAuth flow
Use strong COOKIE_SECRET (32+ random characters) for state signing
Configure CORS origins to restrict to known Sentry domains
Monitor OAuth error metrics for invalid_token patterns

keyTakeaways: Sentry MCP (751 stars, actively maintained) has a robust multi-layer security architecture: OAuth wrapping, session narrowing, SSRF protection, and tool hint annotations
The two-tier auth model (MCP OAuth wrapping Sentry OAuth) means clients never see raw Sentry credentials — a strong security property
Prompt injection protection is still in progress: PR #1056 (untrusted data boundary) and PR #1045 (structured results) are open with known bypasses
The Claude Code plugin's auto-delegation model creates an automated attack surface — no human review before Sentry MCP tools are invoked
Safe setup requires defense-in-depth: OAuth configuration + tool exposure narrowing + monitoring + embedded agent provider isolation
SSRF protection via validateRegionUrl() is well-implemented with allowlist-based domain restriction
The embedded agent provider configuration is a critical security control — always set EMBEDDED_AGENT_PROVIDER explicitly to prevent silent provider switching
Tool hint annotations (PR #1144) are being enforced — part of broader MCP security hardening that will improve safety over time
Monitoring setup follows OpenTelemetry semantic conventions with proper error classification (skip expected errors, always log 5xx/network failures)
